interconnectors.name: Eastern Green Link 1 (Torness to Hawthorn Pit)

ai_summary:
Scotland’s electrical grid is currently operating under exceptional green dispatch conditions, driven by a commanding 4.4 GW of wind generation that anchors regional supply. This massive renewable influx has depressed Scottish carbon intensity to a remarkably clean 32 gCO2/kWh, virtually eliminating fossil-fuel generation across the domestic generation mix and reinforcing the region's role as a primary clean power exporter to the broader British system.

However, this generation surplus continues to collide with physical transmission limitations. Total wasted energy currently registers at 217.5 MWh, reflecting active localized curtailment as cross-border interconnectors reach boundary limits. While regional demand is thoroughly covered by clean electrons, structural bottlenecks—notably across the B6 boundary—prevent the seamless evacuation of low-marginal-cost power southward. Consequently, the system is forced into costly constraint actions, shedding high-value green energy rather than displacing carbon-intensive generation elsewhere on the grid.

To capture this trapped economic and environmental value, priority must be given to accelerating transmission reinforcements, alongside the rapid integration of co-located utility-scale storage and flexible demand mechanisms. Until transmission bandwidth expands in step with offshore and onshore capacity, curtailment figures of this scale will remain an ongoing friction point.
